newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler sets higher Q2 production forecast.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler sets higher Q2 production forecast.

text.p: Chrysler Corp on Tuesday set a second quarter worldwide production forecast of 809,000 units, a 4.3 percent increase from the 775,800 units it produced in the second quarter of 1996.
The company also lowered by 6,900 units its projected output for the first quarter to 765,700.
The company expects to make 244,700 cars in North America and 564,300 trucks in North America and Austria. A year ago, Chrysler produced 269,200 cars and 506,600 trucks.
For the first quarter, Chrysler said it now expects to build 217,300 cars and 548,400 trucks. It previously had forecast to make 218,800 cars and 553,800 trucks.

Chrysler is the only one of the Big Three automakers that has set a production forecast higher than the year ago. Ford Motor Co said last week it expects to make 1,202,000 vehicles in the second period, a decline of less than one percent.
Also last week, General Motors Corp said it expects to make 1,550,000 vehicles in North America, a number about flat with the year-ago period.
